definitions.explanation: A dog without an owner that wanders freely. Can also be used figuratively to describe a person who belongs to no group or organization.

examples.japanese: {野良犬|のらいぬ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{近|ちか}づく→近づく：01958_chikazuku⟧な。
⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{野良犬|のらいぬ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}かけて→見かける：01644_mikakeru⟧{保健所|ほけんじょ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{連絡|れんらく}した→連絡する：20202_renrakusuru⟧。
examples.english: I spotted a stray dog in the park and contacted the public health center.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{野良犬|のらいぬ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ほとんど→ほとんど：00847_hotondo⟧⟦{見|み}かけなく→見かける：01644_mikakeru⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: There used to be many stray dogs, but nowadays you hardly ever see them.

notes:
USAGE:
{野良|のら} means "stray" or "feral" and combines with animal names: {野良犬|のらいぬ} (stray dog), ⟦{野良猫|のらねこ}→野良猫：14440_noraneko⟧ (stray cat). {野良|のら} alone originally means "field" or "open land" and also appears in {野良仕事|のらしごと} (farm work).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {野良犬|のらいぬ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{保護|ほご}する→保護する：25374_hogosuru⟧ (to rescue a stray dog)
- {野良犬|のらいぬ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{噛|か}まれる→噛む：01205_kamu⟧ (to be bitten by a stray dog)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Stray dogs have become rare in modern Japan due to strict animal control laws and active efforts by {保健所|ほけんじょ} (public health centers). In contrast, ⟦{野良猫|のらねこ}→野良猫：14440_noraneko⟧ (stray cats) are still commonly seen.
